theme: The glory departs from the Temple
readingInstruction: Read Ezekiel 8:1-11:25. In a vision, Ezekiel is carried to Jerusalem and sees the idolatry inside the temple. Then the glory of the LORD leaves. Read it slowly, and let the departure of the glory register. Then read the promise at the end of chapter 11.
settingTheScene: In 592 BC, Ezekiel is sitting in his house with the elders of Judah when the Spirit lifts him up in a vision to the temple in Jerusalem. He sees four abominations, each worse than the last. Then the glory of the LORD, which had dwelt in the temple since Solomon dedicated it, rises from the cherubim and moves out of the city. This is the central event of the first part of Ezekiel.
observation: “Son of man, do you see what they are doing, the great abominations that the house of Israel are committing here, to drive me far from my sanctuary?” (8:6).
“Every form of creeping things and loathsome beasts, and all the idols of the house of Israel, engraved on the wall all around” (8:10).
“They say, The LORD does not see us, the LORD has forsaken the land” (8:12).
“Behold, there sat women weeping for Tammuz” (8:14).
“Mark the foreheads of the men who sigh and groan over all the abominations that are committed in it” (9:4).
“Then the glory of the LORD went out from the threshold of the house” (10:18).
“And I will give them one heart, and a new spirit I will put within them. I will remove the heart of stone from their flesh and give them a heart of flesh” (11:19).
“And the glory of the LORD went up from the midst of the city and stood on the mountain that is on the east side of the city” (11:23).
interpretation:
Ezekiel is shown four scenes of corruption in the temple. First, an idol of jealousy at the north gate. Second, seventy elders of Israel offering incense to carved creatures on the walls, saying, “The LORD does not see us.” Third, women weeping for Tammuz, a fertility god. Fourth, twenty-five men with their backs to the temple, bowing to the sun in the east. The leaders, the priests, the women, and the men are all involved. The house built for the worship of the one true God is a pantheon of idols.

God’s response is judgment. In chapter 9, a man in linen marks the foreheads of those who grieve over the abominations. They will be spared. Then others follow to strike. It is a picture of discerning judgment. Even in the midst of destruction, God knows those who are his.

Then comes the heartbreaking departure of the glory. In chapter 10, Ezekiel sees the cherubim and wheels again, and the glory of the LORD rises from the threshold. It moves in stages: from the cherubim to the threshold, to the east gate, up from the city and onto the Mount of Olives. It is an act of reluctant departure. The glory leaves slowly. It is as though God lingers, hoping that they will turn.

In the midst of judgment, in chapter 11, the promise breaks through. God will gather them from the nations. He will remove the heart of stone and give a heart of flesh, with one heart and a new spirit. “Then they will be my people, and I will be their God.” Even though the temple is empty, he promises to be “a sanctuary for a little while” in the countries where they have gone.

This is the theological center: the presence of God is not tied to a building. And it points forward to a day when God’s glory will return, not to a stone temple but to a people with new hearts.
connection: John 1:14 says the Word became flesh and “tabernacled” among us, and we have seen his glory. The glory that left the temple through the east gate stood on the Mount of Olives. Jesus ascended from the Mount of Olives (Acts 1:9-12) and will return there (Zechariah 14:4). 1 Corinthians 3:16 says that believers are God’s temple. Revelation 7:3 and 9:4 echo the sealing of foreheads. 2 Corinthians 3:3 says we are a letter written on hearts of flesh.
application:
Ask what “idols in the temple” might be in your life: hidden things you do where you think God does not see.

Remember that God knows those who sigh and groan over sin. Do you grieve over sin in your own life and in the world?

Thank God that he has taken away your heart of stone and given a heart of flesh. Ask him to keep it soft.
prayerPrompts: Confess the idols in your heart.
Ask him to give you a heart that grieves over sin.
Thank him that he sees all that you do.
